//LocalApi: v3.5+ — SOLO MODE. Off by default. When on, the node serves the coordinator's client-facing API itself (/api/* Ollama dialect and /v1/* OpenAI dialect, blocking and streaming), so a single machine needs one process instead of two: set Coordinator:Enabled=false and point any OpenAI client at Urls below by changing base_url and nothing else. Binds LOOPBACK by default; a non-loopback address with no ApiKeys refuses to start, because an unauthenticated inference endpoint hands arbitrary GPU time to anyone who can reach the port — AllowAnonymous=true is the explicit override for a trusted network. NOT included: the admin API, the console and /metrics — all of which need a fleet. Retrieval IS available since v3.6 but is a separate opt-in; see LocalApi:Retrieval below. Node:MaxConcurrency, advisory when a hub is respecting it, is ENFORCED here: over the cap a request waits MaxWaitSeconds then gets 503 + Retry-After, exactly like the hub's queue.

LocalApi.//Retrieval: v3.6+ — RAG on a standalone node. Off by default. When on, this node ingests documents, indexes them and grounds its own answers: POST /api/collections/{c}/documents to ingest (text, Markdown, HTML, JSON), POST /api/collections/{c}/search to see what retrieves, and X-InferHub-Retrieve on /api/chat, /api/generate or /v1/chat/completions to ground an answer — the same headers, the same augmented prompt and the same X-InferHub-Sources as a coordinator. REQUIRES Coordinator:Enabled=false and fails startup otherwise: a meshed node already holds vector replicas derived from its hub, and a second authoritative store in the same process would be two sources of truth for one collection name. NOT included: PDF (the extractor ships with the coordinator only, so a PDF upload is a clean 415 rather than a bad extraction), and the postgres/qdrant providers (the local store is the only one here). The corpus lands in DataDirectory — in Docker that is /data/retrieval, so mount a volume or it is ephemeral.

Retrieval.//DefaultEmbeddingModel: Resolved against THIS node's backend. A model it does not serve is a 404 naming the model, not a silent empty result.

Retrieval.//OnMissing: 'error' (default) or 'passthrough' — what a chat request does when retrieval cannot run. 'passthrough' answers ungrounded, so choose it deliberately.
Retrieval.//Rerank: 'none' (default) | 'llm'. Costs one extra backend round trip; every failure keeps the original order.

//Coordinator: Enabled (v3.5+) — set false to run without a mesh at all; the node then needs no Url and no EnrollmentSecret, and never dials out. Coordinator:Enabled=false together with LocalApi:Enabled=false fails startup: a node that neither joins a mesh nor serves anyone is a typo.

Coordinator.//EnrollmentSecret: Set via env (Coordinator__EnrollmentSecret) or user-secrets. Must match the coordinator's Auth:NodeEnrollmentSecret.

Node.Name: local-node
Node.//MaxConcurrency: Advisory cap reported to the coordinator. null = unbounded.
Node.//Labels: Free-form key/value pairs surfaced on the coordinator's node snapshot.

Models.//Include: Empty = advertise everything the backend reports.
Models.//Exclude: Names matched here are dropped from the report.

Node.//Capabilities: v3.8+. What this node is routed FOR, as opposed to which models it holds. The node declares its capabilities from what is actually loaded — an Ollama or OpenAI backend means 'chat' and 'embed' over every model it reports — and this key is SUBTRACTIVE only: Disabled: ["chat"] is how you say 'this box is for embeddings', which is the one thing the node cannot work out for itself (Ollama does not say what a model is for, and guessing from names would be a registry that is wrong for somebody). A disabled capability is not routed to it in a mesh and is refused with 503 + Retry-After in solo mode — same key, same meaning, whichever is enforcing it. Disabling both fails startup: a node routed for nothing is a box burning power for nothing.
Node.//Vram: v3.16+ — HOW MUCH OF THIS BOX'S CARD MAY BE SPENT ON MODELS. Unset (0) means no gate at all, which is v3.15's behaviour exactly. When you set it, an image recipe that cannot fit in BudgetMiB minus ReserveMiB is NOT DECLARED — the fleet never routes at it — and one that would fit but does not right now waits on the tool queue and then gets the same 503 + Retry-After as every other limit here. Never an out-of-memory error inside somebody's job, which is what this replaces. DECLARED, NOT DETECTED, and that is deliberate: under WSL2 there are no /dev/nvidia* device nodes, the host's nvidia-smi cannot see the VM's VRAM, and the only reliable signal that a GPU exists at all is that libcuda.so.1 loads — so a node that guessed would guess wrong on the most common GPU-with-Docker setup there is. A budget that is usually right is worse than one that is explicitly absent, because the first failure is an OOM at 2am rather than a startup message. The worker reports what it measures and the node LOGS a disagreement; it never overrides you.

Vram.//BudgetMiB: Total VRAM to plan around, in MiB. 0 = no gate. On a 24 GB card, 24576.
Vram.//ReserveMiB: Held back for the inference backend and the display. With maxWorkers:1 the common case is one recipe loaded at a time, so this key is really about the SECOND thing on the card — an :ollama container holding a chat model beside the :diffusion one. A reserve at or above the budget fails startup: it is not a strict configuration, it is one that can never admit anything.

//Tools: v3.9+ — TOOL WORKERS. Off by default. When on, the node can start child processes that do work its inference backend cannot: transcription, speech, anything you write. A manifest in ManifestDirectory says what a tool can do and how to start it (see python/README.md for the format and the line protocol); the node spawns it, talks to it over stdin/stdout, restarts it when it dies, and declares its capabilities to the coordinator so (capability, model) routing finds it. Reachable at POST /api/tools/{capability} on a hub and on a solo node alike. OPT IN TWICE: Enabled consents to the feature, and Allowed names the manifest ids that may actually run — a manifest on disk that is not in the list is loaded, logged and never started. The two are not redundant: from v3.11 a coordinator can turn a node's capabilities on and off, and Allowed is the ceiling it can never raise. THIS IS NOT A SANDBOX: a worker runs as the node's user, with the node's filesystem and the node's network. The node drops its own environment before spawning (a worker gets PATH, HOME, LANG, TMPDIR and whatever the manifest's 'env' names — never Coordinator__EnrollmentSecret), and that is the honest extent of the isolation. Run a tool you did not write in its own container and point a manifest at it.

Tools.//Allowed: Manifest ids this node may run. Empty with Enabled=true starts nothing and says so at boot, which is a legitimate way to stage a rollout. Naming tools while Enabled is false FAILS STARTUP: reading your own list back and concluding it is on is the mistake this catches.
Tools.//ScratchDirectory: Per-request working directories, created and deleted in a finally — always, after success and after failure. Attachments go here as files rather than through the pipe, and a request's bytes never outlive it. In Docker this is /data/tools/scratch, so mount a volume.
Tools.//MaxAttachmentBytes: 25 MB, matching what the OpenAI audio API accepts. Over it is a 413 at the edge naming the limit, before anything is buffered onward. This is the BUFFERED path — the bytes arrive on the job. Since v3.21 it is one of two ceilings; see MaxStreamedBytes.
Tools.//MaxStreamedBytes: v3.21+ — the ceiling for an upload that STREAMS through the hub instead of being buffered in it. 0 is off, and off is the default: a node that changes nothing here is routed exactly as v3.20 was and refuses exactly what it did. Set it and this node declares SupportsStreamedAttachments, which is what a hub filters on before sending it a streamed job — one key, so a node cannot advertise something it will then refuse. It must be 0 or at least MaxAttachmentBytes; a streamed ceiling below the buffered one can only refuse a request the buffered path would have taken. THE TRADE: a streamed job is NOT retried on another node, because the body has already been read and a client's socket cannot be rewound, so a node lost mid-upload is a 502 the caller has to act on. Applies to POST /api/tools/{capability} and /v1/audio/transcriptions — the image routes stay buffered, because a phase-47 image job is answered before it runs and its bytes would have to outlive the request.
Tools.//AllowModelDownload: v3.10+ — may a worker fetch model weights it does not have? Off by default, and it is a THIRD opt-in on purpose: Enabled consents to running tools, Allowed consents to running these tools, and this consents to one of them reaching the internet from a box you may have deliberately air-gapped (Whisper auto-downloads on first use). With it off, a worker that needs missing weights fails the JOB with a message naming this key and the exact pre-fetch command; the node keeps serving everything else. The inferhub-node:tools image sets it true, because choosing that image is the consent.
Tools.//QueueMaxWaitSeconds: How long a request waits for a free worker before 503 + Retry-After — the same shape as the hub's queue and solo mode's concurrency gate, so a client's retry logic behaves identically whichever limit it hit.
Tools.//CancelGraceSeconds: v3.15+ — how long a worker gets to honour a `cancel` frame before it is terminated and restarted. Killing it immediately would be simpler and is wrong: a diffusion worker holds weights that took tens of seconds to load, so killing it to abandon ONE job punishes the NEXT caller, and the punishment gets worse with every model your catalogue gains. Past this budget the worker is by definition not cooperating and is terminated.
Tools.//MaxStartAttempts: The restart budget, lifted from Ollama:Supervisor. Past it a tool's pool stops starting workers, logs once at Error, WITHDRAWS ITS CAPABILITIES from this node's registration so the coordinator stops routing that work here, and keeps probing every RecoveryProbeInterval — so a fix is noticed without a restart.
Tools.//Image: v3.14+ — keys the IMAGE worker honours. Every one of them is read by the worker; the node's job is only to state them into the child's environment, because the environment is cleared before spawn. Inert unless an image worker is loaded.

Image.//RequireGpu: Default TRUE: the worker refuses to start when no CUDA device is reachable, and says which key to unset. That is a refusal rather than a slow path on purpose — a tool that loads happily on a CPU and then serves four-minute requests is a node the fleet keeps routing to, and every caller pays for the discovery. Unset it and only recipes marked cpuViable are offered (sd15 at 512x512 is tens of seconds; sdxl at 1024x1024 is minutes).
Image.//AllowSlowCpu: Offer the CPU-hostile recipes on a CPU-only box anyway. Your hardware, your call — with a warning. Off.
Image.//RecipeDirectory: Where model recipes live. A RECIPE is a model (repo, pinned revision, aspect buckets, defaults); a MANIFEST is a tool. They are two files on purpose: the manifest is your ceiling and is what Tools:Allowed names, while recipes are a catalogue the tool reads — so a coordinator profile can turn a model on without you having pre-named it. Empty means the worker's default, which in the :diffusion image is /opt/inferhub/recipes. From v3.16 the NODE reads this directory too, for exactly three fields — the id, the licence and the VRAM figure — because the profile clamp has to refuse an oversized or unlicensed recipe with no worker running.
Image.//AcceptedLicenses: v3.16+ — LICENCE IDS YOU HAVE READ AND ACCEPTED. A recipe whose license.permissive is not true is loaded, logged by name and NOT STARTED unless its licence id is in this list; the log line names the licence and links to the text. This is a FOURTH opt-in and it is not redundant: Enabled consents to the feature, Allowed consents to these tools, AllowModelDownload consents to reaching the internet, and none of them says 'and I accept the Stability AI Non-Commercial Research Community License'. A list rather than a boolean for the same reason Allowed is one — sd35-medium is free for most people who will run it and sdxl-turbo is not usable commercially at all, so one flag would let somebody who read one licence enable both. Of what ships, sd35-medium (stabilityai-ai-community) and sdxl-turbo (sai-nc-community) need it; the other four do not. An entry set to "" is ignored, which is how you clear one that came from an image. None of this is legal advice — it is a refusal to make that call for you, silently.
Image.//ResidentRecipes: v3.16+ — how many models may be on the card at once. Default 1. Switching recipes SWAPS weights inside the warm process rather than restarting it, because a restart pays the interpreter and the import of torch on top of the weights; with more than one resident, a box that alternates between two models stops thrashing entirely. A 48 GB card genuinely can hold SDXL and FLUX together. The default is 1 because the expensive default is the one nobody realises they chose.
Image.//HuggingFaceToken: v3.16+ — a read token for a GATED repository; of what ships, only sd35-medium needs one. It has to be a key here rather than an HF_TOKEN environment variable because the node CLEARS the child's environment before spawn, so a variable set on the container reaches the node and stops there. It is a separate thing from AcceptedLicenses, and conflating them would be wrong in both directions: accepting a licence tells THIS NODE it may run a model, and a token is how HUGGING FACE decides whether to hand the weights over. Empty means none is sent — an empty token is not the same as no token, and sending a blank one gets a 401 on a repo that would have been readable anonymously.
Image.//SeamWarnThreshold: v3.17+ — above this, an equirectangular result carries a 'seam' warning. Default 0.08, and it is the mean absolute difference between the image's first and last columns, 0-1, which is the pair that becomes adjacent once a 360 panorama is wrapped onto a sphere. It is a WARNING and never a failure: a slightly visible seam is your own problem and your own aesthetic judgement, and failing a two-minute job over a metric threshold would be the tool overriding you about a picture only you can see. And the seam is never REPAIRED — a roll-and-inpaint fix is a second generation pass you did not ask for, did not watch, and would be billed for; upstream ships one and it is a good tool to reach for deliberately. Set to 0 to silence the warning without silencing the measurement, which is reported on every equirectangular result whatever this says.

//Images: v3.14+ — what the IMAGE EDGE accepts, before a single diffusion step runs. The coordinator binds the same section into the same class, so a request refused on a hub is refused identically on a solo node.

Images.//MaxBatch: The absolute ceiling on `n`, whatever the size. A batch runs on ONE node — fanning it across nodes would mean four different seeds' worth of scheduling for a request a client thinks is atomic, and a partial failure would have no honest status.
Images.//MaxResponseBytes: An upper bound on everything one request may send back, estimated as width x height x 4 x n before anything runs. CLAMPED BY Tools:MaxAttachmentBytes at use: that cap is what sizes the mesh's SignalR message limit, and exceeding a SignalR limit tears the connection down rather than failing the message. Raising this without raising that gets you no change, deliberately.
Images.//MaxRequestBytes: v3.18+ — what one EDIT may send in: the picture and the mask together, refused with a 413 before anything is buffered onward. Each part is also capped by Tools:MaxAttachmentBytes.
Images.//SyncMaxWaitSeconds: v3.15+ — read by the coordinator only; a solo node's synchronous image route has no queue in front of it. Left here so the two hosts bind one section into one class.
Images.//Jobs: v3.15+ — the async surface at POST /api/images/jobs, served by this node itself when it has an image worker. Same five routes and same bodies as a coordinator's. Nothing persists and NOTHING TOUCHES DISK; a restart forgets every job.

Jobs.//MaxQueueDepth: A standalone node runs ONE image job at a time — it is a box with a card in it, and letting two into a pool sized maxWorkers:1 would only move the queue one layer down where it has no position to report. This is how many may wait behind that one.

//Backend: Type — 'ollama' (default) or 'openai'. 'openai' drives any server speaking the OpenAI wire format: vLLM, llama.cpp's server, LM Studio, TGI, or a hosted provider. It reads the OpenAi section below.
//Ollama: RequestTimeout — how long to wait on a single Ollama call. Defaults to 5 minutes to match the coordinator's Dispatcher:TimeoutSeconds; HttpClient's own default is only 100s, which a cold large model blows through. Raise it for very large models.

Ollama.//RequireGpu: v3.7+. Off by default, INCLUDING in the bundled image (ghcr.io/dev-art-solutions/inferhub-node:ollama), which supports a CPU-only mode on purpose — embedding models and small models run fine on a CPU. Every node logs what CUDA it can see at startup either way, so the failure this guards against is not 'no GPU' but 'no GPU and nobody said so'. Turn it on for a node whose whole purpose is the card: with no visible device it then fails startup naming --gpus all, rather than quietly becoming fifty times slower because a flag fell out of a unit file.
Ollama.//Supervisor: v3.4+. Off by default. When on, the node probes its own Ollama every ProbeInterval on a short deadline of its own (ProbeTimeout — NOT RequestTimeout above, or a wedged Ollama would take 15 minutes to notice) and, after UnhealthyThreshold consecutive failures, restarts it: connection refused = start it, accepts-but-never-answers = stop it first, then start. LOOPBACK ONLY — a remote or shared Ollama, or Backend:Type=openai, disables it with one log line, because somebody else's inference server is not this node's to bounce. Restarts are budgeted (MaxRestartAttempts per RestartWindow, RestartBackoff doubling); past the budget it stops restarting, says so once at Error, and keeps probing so a recovery is still picked up. A restart aborts whatever was streaming through this node.
Ollama.//Supervisor.StartAtBoot: v3.7+. Off by default. On, the node probes once at startup and — only if nothing is listening at all — starts Ollama immediately instead of waiting out UnhealthyThreshold probes first. For a deployment that OWNS its Ollama and knows it is not running yet, which is the bundled container; on an ordinary box the wait is right, because a node and its Ollama usually boot together. Never applies to a wedge: something already answering the port at boot is exactly where starting it again fails on a bound port and the log blames the wrong thing.
Ollama.//Supervisor.StopOnShutdown: v3.7+. Off by default. On, the node stops the Ollama IT SPAWNED when it shuts down — never a service, never one that was already running. Off is right on a desktop, where you may still be using that Ollama after stopping the node; on is right in a container, where the child gets SIGKILLed the moment PID 1 exits and a stop mid-'ollama pull' leaves a partial blob behind.
Ollama.//Supervisor.AutoInstall: A SECOND, separate opt-in: Enabled consents to restarting a process, not to downloading and running an installer. Fires only when neither a service nor a binary is found (i.e. 'not installed', never 'not answering'), once per process lifetime, with the exact command logged before it runs. Set InstallUrl to a mirror for an air-gapped or policy-managed fleet.

//OpenAi: Used only when Backend:Type=openai, and then BaseUrl is REQUIRED — the node refuses to start without it. ApiKey must come from env (OpenAi__ApiKey) or user-secrets, never from this file. Models:Include is effectively mandatory against a hosted provider: its catalogue is hundreds of models this node cannot serve, and reporting them all makes the coordinator route anything here.
